correctness.rationale: PASS: For friendship graph F_n, each triangle base edge has two spoke neighbours and forces its spoke colours to differ. For a spoke edge colour beta and test colour alpha, adjacent alpha count is S_alpha - 1_{alpha=beta} + 1_{alpha=c_i} out of 2n neighbouring edges. Since a fixed alpha occurs at most once in each triangle, S_alpha<=n; the only possible violation is choosing a base colour alpha with S_alpha=n. Thus each triangle base has q-k available colours where k=0,1,2 are universally present spoke colours. Inclusion-exclusion on q(q-1) ordered spoke pairs per triangle gives A0,A1,A2 and P_n(q)=q^n A0+(q-1)^n A1+(q-2)^n A2. P_n(2)=0 and fixed pair of spoke colours plus a third base colour works, so index is 3; this index was previously known.

evidence: Eulerian |E| divisible by 3 gives the known index <=3; later papers give uniform existence bounds and minimum-degree effects. No inspected statement furnishes P_n(q) for all n>=1,q>=2.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A bound on the least palette size is weaker than the entire distribution of valid colour assignments and cannot dominate the count without further combinatorics.

originality.rationale: PASS (best of knowledge): Kalinowski et al Proposition21 already implies index three for Eulerian friendship graph with 3n edges, and Antoniuk et al and Pękała–Przybyło improve general upper bounds. Those existence theorems are expressly credited and do not imply the full labelled-palette counting polynomial, with every number q of named colours. The universal-spoke-colour filtration is a new exact counting detail in the bounded comparisons.
